blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Forming an accurate theory-of-mind (ToM) is key to successful multi-agent collaboration and requires reasoning under uncertainty to capture multiple possible partner states. This is hard to do in the text representation space native to large language model (LLM) agents, which more easily describe a single partner state. To address this challenge, we introduce ToM2Vec, which learns to form abstract theories-of-mind in a rich latent space via a fixed budget of continuous reasoning tokens. During training, supervision for these tokens comes from the partner's actual thoughts, which the ToM tokens are trained to abstract and match. At test-time, ToM tokens are generated by each agent and act as conditioners for that agent's thoughts and actions. Across several environments covering collaborative, competitive, and mixed-motive settings (Overcooked-AI, multiparty negotiation, Decrypto, Hanabi, and Collab Escape/Capture), we evaluate ToM2Vec's ability to support multi-agent interactions and collaboration, finding consistent improvements over the base model and a variety of competitive trained and prompted baselines. We show that latent reasoning is critical, with performance dropping when reasoning is expressed in text. Moreover, we show that ToM2Vec training generalizes to partner model families not seen at train-time, including a proprietary model (GPT-5.4). In our analysis, we provide evidence that the latent tokens encode a ToM, rather than task-specific information: ToM2Vec's tokens improve the agent's ability to directly answer questions about partner beliefs, desires, and next actions.
blocks.zh: 形成准确的 " 注意 " (Tom)理论是成功开展多代理人协作的关键,需要在不确定的情况下进行推理,以抓住多个可能的伙伴国家。 这在文字代表空间中很难做到,在大语言模型(LLM)代理中更方便地描述单个伙伴国. 为了应对这一挑战,我们引入了TOM2Vec,它通过固定的连续推理符号预算,在丰富的潜在空间中学习形成抽象的思维理论. 在训练期间,对这些道具的监督来自合伙人的实际想法,TOM道具经过了抽象和相配的训练. 在测试时,每个代理都会生成Tom符,并充当该代理的思想和行动调节器. 在整个涵盖协作、竞争和混合动机环境的多个环境(监督-AI、多方谈判、Decrypto、Hanabi和Collab Escape/Capture)中,我们评价了TOM2Vec支持多代理人互动和协作的能力,发现在基础模式和各种经过培训的竞争性基线方面不断改进。 我们表明,潜在的推理至关重要,当推理在文本中表达时,表现会下降。 此外,我们显示,TOM2Vec培训向在火车时刻没有见到的伙伴模范家庭进行概括,包括一种专有模式(GPT-5.4)。 在我们的分析中,我们提供了证据,说明潜伏的活符编码了一个Tom,而不是特定任务的信息:TOM2Vec的活符提高了代理商直接回答关于伙伴信仰,欲望和下一步行动的问题的能力.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Humans have the ability to coordinate with each other remarkably well, often with little or no explicit communication. For instance, chefs can prepare a meal together, teammates can execute a play, and negotiators can converge on a deal, each anticipating what the other will do and acting accordingly. This capacity for joint action rests on each agent’s Theory of Mind (ToM): the ability to model another agent’s unobserved mental state based on observed behaviors ( Premack and Woodruff, 1978 ) .
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents that must act alongside partner agents (human or AI) in both collaborative and competitive tasks ( Duan et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Stengel-Eskin et al., 2024 ; Kosinski, 2024 ; Xu et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ; Xiao et al., 2026 ) . To succeed in these settings, an agent needs strong working ToM ( Bakhtin et al., 2022 ; Li et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2025a ) .
This ToM allows the agent to infer a partner’s goals, beliefs, and likely next actions, enabling it to coordinate with less explicit communication and adapt to a counterpart’s strategy on the fly ( Baker et al., 2009 ; Wu et al., 2020 ) .
blocks.zh:
人类能够很好地相互协调,往往很少或没有明确的沟通。 例如,厨师们可以一起准备一顿饭,队友们可以执行一出戏,谈判者可以就一项交易达成共识,每个人都可以预料对方会做什么,并相应采取行动。 这种联合行动的能力取决于每个代理商的Mind(Tom)理论:根据观察到的行为来模拟另一个代理商未观察的精神状态的能力(Premack和Woodruff,1978年)。
越来越多的大型语言模型(LLMS)作为代理人,在协作和竞争任务中必须与伙伴代理人(人或AI)一起行动(Duan等人,2024年;Chen等人,2024年;Stengel-Eskin等人,2024年;Kosinski,2025年)。 2024; 徐等, 2024; 周等, 2025; 萧等, 2026. 为了在这些环境中取得成功,一个特工需要强大的工作TOM(Bakhtin等人,2022年;Li等人,2023年;Chen等人,2025年a).
这个TOM允许代理人推断一个伙伴的目标、信仰以及可能的未来行动,使其能够与不太明确的沟通进行协调,并适应对应方的苍蝇战略(Baker等人,2009年;Wu等人,2020年)。

blocks.en:
Making these kinds of inferences can be seen as a form of world modeling directed at another agent ( Raileanu et al., 2018 ; Xie et al., 2021 ; Yu et al., 2022 ; Chernyavskiy et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) .
As in world modeling, it is often important to form an abstract model that can superimpose multiple possibilities, in this case of the partner’s intent Xie et al. (2021) ; Chernyavskiy et al. (2025) .
A general sketch of the partner’s beliefs and intentions is often sufficient, and excessive fidelity can be inefficient and in fact harmful to the task ( Mu et al., 2026 ) ; for example, when two chefs have to coordinate in a crowded kitchen, one does not need to predict what the other wants for breakfast tomorrow (which might even be a distraction), but does need to predict if the other needs shared resources.
blocks.zh:
做出这些推论可以看作是一种针对另一种物剂的世界建模形式(Raileanu等人,2018年;谢等人,2021年;Yu等人,2022年;Chernyavskiy等人,2025年;张等人,2025年).
和世界建模一样,形成一个可以叠加多种可能性的抽象模型也往往很重要,在这种情况下,伴侣的意向是谢等人(2021年);切尔尼亚夫斯基等人(2025年).
对伴侣的信仰和意图作一概括描述往往就足够了,过度的忠诚可能效率低下,事实上对任务有害(Mu等人,2026年);例如,当两位厨师必须在拥挤的厨房里协调时,一个人不需要预测其他人明天早餐想要什么(这甚至可能是分散注意力),而是需要预测其他厨师是否需要共享资源.

blocks.en:
Given this goal of abstraction, a key challenge for ToM agents lies in building an abstract representation
that retains enough information about the partner’s potential future paths to support prediction and planning, while lifting unnecessary details.
We argue that natural language is a poor medium for this kind of abstraction, as expressing another agent’s intent or state linguistically tends to commit the agent to a single estimate of the partner, even when many distinct hypotheses are possible.
Instead, we argue that modeling another agent may be more akin to forming a latent world model ( LeCun, 2022 ) ,
where abstractions are formed in the model’s latent space rather than its output space (see Figure 1 ).
Latent reasoning paradigms offer precisely this kind of latent-space abstraction as a natural alternative to verbalized reasoning,
where latent thought tokens can superimpose several candidate chains-of-thought rather than fixing to one ( Hao et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025b ; Shi et al., 2026 ) .
Similarly, we argue that a representation of a partner should be able to superimpose multiple hypotheses about the partner’s goals and intentions, and that a ToM agent should be able to predict these representations and consider alternatives before committing to a decision.
blocks.zh:
鉴于这一抽象目标,Tom代理公司面临的一个关键挑战在于建立抽象的代表制度。
保留足够的关于伙伴未来可能路径的信息,以支持预测和规划,同时取消不必要的细节。
我们主张,自然语言是这种抽象的不良媒介,因为表达另一个代理人的意图或状态在语言上倾向于将代理人用于对伴侣的单一估计,即使许多不同的假设是可能的。
相反,我们争论说,模拟另一个物剂可能更类似于形成潜在的世界模型(LeCun, 2022年),
在模型潜在空间而不是其输出空间中形成抽象之处(见图1)。
原始推理范式 恰恰提供了这种潜在的空间抽象 作为自然替代 口头推理,
(Hao等人,2025年;Li等人,2025年;Chen等人,2025年b;Shi等人,2026年)
同样,我们主张,一个伙伴的代表应该能够超越关于伙伴目标和意图的多种假设,而一个Tom代理应该能够预测这些陈述,并在对决定作出承诺之前考虑其他选择。

blocks.en:
To this end, we introduce ToM2Vec to directly learn these latent representations of the partner agent. ToM2Vec trains the agent to predict, from its own point-of-view, a fixed number of continuous latent embeddings that abstract over its partner’s thoughts; in other words, it teaches the main agent to perform a mind-reading task about its partner.
During training, we obtain supervision for these latent embeddings by abstracting a training partner’s actual next thoughts into continuous latent tokens to serve as a representation of its reasoning.
We train the agent’s generated latent embeddings to match the partner’s hidden states under a cosine similarity objective (see Figure 2 );
during training, we use the same model for both agent and partner, as their representation spaces must be shared.
At test-time (where partner reasoning is not available) an agent trained with ToM2Vec then generates its own latent thought tokens, intended to capture a ToM about the partner.
Interestingly, we show that at test-time, our training generalizes to other partner models, including a closed-source proprietary model that is stronger than the training partner.
blocks.zh:
为此,我们引入TOM2Vec直接学习伙伴代理人的这些潜在表述. ToM2Vec训练代理商从自己的视角预测一定数量的连续潜伏嵌入物,这些潜入物会抽象地超越其伙伴的思想;换句话说,它教主要代理商执行关于伙伴的读心任务.
在培训期间,我们通过将培训伙伴的下一个实际想法抽象为持续的潜在标志来监督这些潜在的嵌入。
我们培训代理人产生的潜伏嵌入物,以配合在同位素相似性目标下的合伙人隐藏状态(见图2);
在培训期间,我们为代理人和伙伴使用同样的模式,因为他们的代表空间必须共享。
在测试时(在无法提供伙伴推理的情况下),受过TOM2Vec训练的特工随后会生成自己的潜伏思维符,意在捕捉关于伙伴的TOM.
有趣的是,我们显示,在试验时,我们的培训向其他伙伴模式概括,包括一个比培训伙伴更强大的封闭源码专有模式。

blocks.en:
We evaluate ToM2Vec across cooperative and competitive tasks, including (1) Overcooked ( Carroll et al., 2019 ) , a cooperative cooking environment, (2) multi-party LLM negotiation ( Abdelnabi et al., 2024 ) , (3) Decrypto ( Lupu et al., 2025 ) , a ToM task where two agents attempt to pass secret messages without being decoded by an interceptor agent, (4) Hanabi ( Agashe et al., 2025 ) , a cooperative card game with hidden information, and (5) Collab Escape/Capture ( Agashe et al., 2025 ) , two collaborative coordination tasks.
Across these domains, ToM2Vec delivers consistent improvements over competitive baselines. Relative to the untrained model (Qwen3-8B), training with ToM2Vec improves the average Overcooked score by 12.0 points and raises negotiation deal success from 62.0% to 71.0%. It also outperforms approaches that prompt agents to consider their partners’ intentions or train them to explicitly verbalize their partners’ reasoning, supporting the value of learning latent partner representations. In Overcooked, these benefits extend to unseen partners from different model families: ToM2Vec improves over the base agent by 17.3 points on average with a GPT-5.4 partner and matches or exceeds the base agent with a Gemma-4 partner, despite training only with a Qwen3-8B partner.
blocks.zh:
我们评价TOM2Vec跨合作和竞争任务,包括(1) 过度烹调(Carroll等人,2019年),一种合作烹饪环境,(2) 多党派LLM谈判(Abdelnabi等人,2024年),(3) Decrypto(Lupu等人,2025年), 这是一项Tom任务,其中两名特工试图传递秘密信息而不由拦截者解码, (4)Hanabi(Agashe等人,2025年),是一款合作牌游戏,有隐藏信息;(5)Collab Escape/Capture(Agashe等人,2025年),两款合作协调任务.
通过这些领域,TOM2Vec在竞争基线方面不断改进。 相对于未经过训练的模式(Qune3-8B),与TOM2Vec进行的培训将平均超熟分提高12.0分,并将谈判交易成功率从62.0%提高到71.0%. 它还超越了促使代理人考虑其伙伴意图或训练其明确表达伙伴推理的方法,支持学习潜在伙伴陈述的价值。 在"超熟"中,这些好处扩展到不同模范家族的隐形伴侣:TOM2Vec在GPT-5.4搭档中平均比基底代理提高17.3分,并且与Gemma-4搭档匹配或超过基底代理,尽管只培训了Qwen3-8B搭档.

blocks.en:
Our analysis further examines to what extent ToM2Vec learns representations that capture a partner’s evolving beliefs. We directly test whether these representations better support inferences about a partner’s beliefs, desires, and next actions (i.e., Baker et al. (2011) ’s Bayesian ToM modeling)
within a given environment state.
We also test whether the latent tokens encode partner-specific reasoning by deliberately corrupting the context used to derive them. Latents derived from the partner’s actual context assign lower perplexity to its true reasoning than those derived from an altered layout or an adversarial intent, supporting the interpretation that they capture context-sensitive information about the partner rather than only generic signals useful for coordination.
We complement this analysis with additional results in the appendix, showing that ToM2Vec helps in Sally-Anne-style false-belief tests, and that the representations learned by ToM2Vec support belief revision given new evidence.
blocks.zh:
我们的分析进一步研究了Tom2Vec在多大程度上学习了能够捕捉伴侣不断变化的信仰的表达. 我们直接测试这些表述是否更好地支持对伴侣信仰、欲望和下一步行动的推论(即Baker等人(2011年)的Bayesian ToM建模)
在特定环境状态下。
我们还通过故意破坏用来推断其背景来检验潜在标志是否为特定伙伴的推理编码。 从伴侣的实际上下文衍生出来的推论,其真实推理比从改变的布局或敌对意图中得出的推论更为复杂,支持这样的解释,即它们捕捉到有关伴侣的上下文敏感信息,而不仅仅是对协调有用的通用信号。
我们用附录中的额外结果来补充这一分析,表明TOM2Vec有助于萨利-安纳式的虚假信仰测试,并且TOM2Vec所学到的表述支持在有新证据的情况下修改信仰.

blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
Figure 2: Overview of ToM2Vec on the multi-party negotiation task. Left (training): From its local observation and interaction history, the main agent predicts K K continuous latent ToM tokens that summarize a partner’s likely reasoning trace. Middle (training): The partner’s reasoning is segmented at sentence delimiters, and latent tokens are extracted across the trace.
These K K vectors provide self-supervised targets for position-wise cosine alignment with the main agent’s predictions. Right (inference): The main agent predicts the latent ToM tokens using only its local context and conditions its subsequent reasoning and action on them. The partner’s private context and reasoning are used only to construct training targets.

blocks.en: 2.2 Modeling Partners via Latent Reasoning
blocks.zh: 2.2 通过Latent Reasoning模拟合作伙伴

blocks.en:
Under partial observability, the main agent must anticipate its partner’s behavior without observing the partner’s complete history and reasoning. We train ℬ θ \mathcal{B}_{\theta} to predict a fixed budget of K K continuous latent vectors from the main agent’s own context: 𝐳 ^ t = ( z ^ t , 1 , … , z ^ t , K ) = Latent K ⁡ ( ℬ θ ; c t M ) , \hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t}=\big(\hat{z}_{t,1},\ldots,\hat{z}_{t,K}\big)=\operatorname{Latent}_{K}(\mathcal{B}_{\theta};c_{t}^{M}), Here, Latent K \operatorname{Latent}_{K} denotes K K autoregressive steps in the model’s hidden space. To perform these steps, we follow recent work on latent reasoning ( Hao et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2025 ) and treat the last layer’s hidden state at each step as the next step’s input embedding, rather than decoding out to the vocabulary.
These latent ToM tokens are intended to summarize the partner’s likely reasoning given what the main agent can observe.

blocks.en: 2.3 Self-Supervised Training via Self-Play
blocks.zh: 2.3 通过自我操作进行自我监督培训

blocks.en:
ToM2Vec operates by teaching agents to predict latent vectors of each other’s thought traces.
To obtain a signal for this, we leverage self-play: given a main agent (to be trained) and a partner agent (both parameterized by the same model ℬ \mathcal{B} ), we sample a reasoning trace from the partner, compress it into latent tokens, and then supervise the main agent to autoregressively produce latent tokens that match the latent tokens extracted from the partner.

blocks.en: 3 Experiments and Results
blocks.zh: 3 实验和结果

blocks.en: 3.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 3.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate ToM2Vec on five multi-agent environments that span cooperative (Overcooked-AI, Hanabi, Collab Escape/Capture), mixed-motive (negotiation), and competitive (Decrypto) multi-agent settings.
Overcooked-AI ( Carroll et al., 2019 ) is a fully cooperative
cooking game in which two agents share a kitchen and must interleave complementary subtasks (e.g., fetching onions, plating, and delivering) to maximize the total team score. We use three layouts provided in Carroll et al. (2019) (Cramped Room, Asymmetric Advantages, and Coordination Ring) each run for 30 seeds.
Multi-party, multi-issue negotiation ( Abdelnabi et al., 2024 ) is a mixed-motive task that we evaluate over 100 samples where each agent holds private preferences over a set of issues and must reach an agreement that balances their own self-interest against the broader risk of walking away with no deal. Decrypto ( Lupu et al., 2025 ) is a competitive
ToM communication game, in which a decoder must interpret a teammate’s clues relating to provided hint words (which only the decoder and teammate can view) while an interceptor simultaneously tries to recover the same hidden code from those clues; we run Decrypto over 1000 samples.
We evaluate multiple environments from the LLM Coordination benchmark ( Agashe et al., 2025 ) .
Hanabi is a cooperative card game in which players can observe their
teammates’ cards but not their own, requiring them to interpret limited
hints to coordinate their actions; we run Hanabi over 100 seeds.
In Collab Capture, two agents
coordinate their movement and actions to capture an adversary.
In Collab Escape, two agents must repair generators to open an exit
while evading an adversary. In all environments, each agent receives only the observation permitted by its role, and cannot see their partners’ private contexts.
Following Agashe et al. (2025) , we evaluate Collab Capture and Collab Escape on 6 and 12 seeds respectively.

blocks.en: 3.2 Metrics
blocks.zh: 3.2 计量

blocks.en:
We report each domain’s standard metrics.
For Overcooked, we report mean episode score.
For LLM Negotiation, we report deal-success rate (deal is acceptable for at least 5/6 parties) together with the agent’s own score and the average collective score across all parties.
For Decrypto, we report the decoder win rate (how often the team guesses the codes), and interceptor win rate (how often the interceptor guesses the codes).
For Hanabi, we report game score, which is the number of correctly played cards.
For Collab Capture and Collab Escape, we report capture and escape success rates, respectively, together with average turn counts, following Agashe et al. (2025) .
A strong ToM agent should improve across these tasks, which each require some form of partner modeling.

blocks.en: 3.3 Baselines
blocks.zh: 3.3 基线

blocks.en:
We compare ToM2Vec to the following baselines: • Untrained Base Model :
the untrained base agent acting on its own context, with no explicit partner modeling. Note that “base” here refers to the untrained nature of this starting point model – in practice, all models used are post-trained. • Prompted ToM : the agent is explicitly prompted to reason about its partner’s observations, goals, and likely next actions before acting. • Language ToM Training : a model trained to verbalize a text summary of the partner’s reasoning (i.e., to decode the partner’s summarized CoT as discrete text), rather than predicting latent ToM tokens.
This isolates the contribution of the latent representation. • Self-Consistency ( Wang et al., 2023 ) : the agent samples three reasoning chains for its next decision and acts on the majority choice. • SimToM ( Wilf et al., 2024 ) : a ToM prompting method in which the agent first recognizes what it knows about the partner, then conditions its own reasoning and action on that inferred perspective. • Adaptive ToM ( Mu et al., 2026 ) : a ToM method for Overcooked in which the agent estimates its partner’s ToM reasoning order based on prior interactions, to improve its own reasoning. • Oracle Partner : an upper bound in which the agent is given the partner’s actual relevant private thoughts (i.e., next action and intent) at inference, obtained from the partner’s next turn.

blocks.en: Overall, the consistency of these results indicates that ToM2Vec learns a partner model that is useful for multi-agent tasks, and that the method generalizes across a wide variety of domains and task configurations.

blocks.en:
Granting the agent oracle access to its partner’s private context raises mean score by 23.0 points over the base model, indicating that accurate partner information provides a strong benefit for coordination in these tasks (see Table 1 ).
Prompting a model to reason explicitly about its partner, however, results in more marginal gains (average gain of 1.7 points)
and even decreases performance on Cramped Room.
Even more advanced prompting methods like SimToM ( Wilf et al., 2024 ) and Adaptive ToM ( Mu et al., 2026 ) provide only marginal gains, underscoring the benefits of training.
blocks.zh:
给予代理人甲骨文进入其伙伴的私人背景,比基准模式提高了23.0分的中分,表明准确的伙伴信息为这些任务的协调提供了很大的好处(见表1)。
然而,促使一个模式明确说明其伙伴的情况,导致收益更微不足道(平均收益1.7分)
更会降低在破烂室的性能
更先进的激励方法如SimTOM(Wilf等人,2024年)和适应TOM(Mu等人,2026年)只能提供边际收益,强调培训的好处.

blocks.en:
Replacing the latent ToM tokens with an explicit natural-language summary of the partner’s reasoning (Language ToM training) recovers only a small part of ToM2Vec ’s gains. For Overcooked, Language ToM training averages 97.6 and trails ToM2Vec on all three layouts by 6.0, 9.0, and 12.3 points (see Table 1 ).
In some instances, latent ToM reasoning succeeds where verbalizing the partner’s reasoning through text fails. Specifically, on Coordination Ring Language ToM training falls 0.7 points below the base model, whereas ToM2Vec improves it by 11.6.
Similar trends can be seen across all other domains; in Collab Escape ( Table 5 ) Language ToM even leads to a 10 percentage point (pp) drop in performance, whereas ToM2Vec improves by 16pp, highlighting the importance of latent thoughts.
blocks.zh:
用明确的自然语言摘要来代替潜在的Tom标志(Language ToM training), 就超熟而言,语言Tom培训平均为97.6,在所有三种布局上跟踪TOM2Vec以6.0,9.0和12.3分(见表1)。
在某些情况下,如果通过文本口头表达伴侣的推理失败,潜在的Tom推理就会成功。 具体来说,在协调环语言Tom培训方面,低于基准模型0.7分,而TOM2Vec则将其改进11.6分.
其它所有领域都可以看到类似的趋势;在Collab Escape(表5)中,语言toM甚至导致性能下降10个百分点(pp),而TOM2Vec则改进了16pp,突出了潜伏思想的重要性.

blocks.en: 4 Discussion and Analysis
blocks.zh: 4. 讨论和分析

blocks.en: Table 6: Overcooked results for partner agents of different architectures across 20 seeds. Each agent is tested with both Qwen3-8B and ToM2Vec . Neither GPT-5.4 nor Gemma-4 were seen during training.
blocks.zh: 表6:20个种子中不同建筑伙伴代理人的超熟结果。 每个剂都用Quen3-8B和TOM2Vec进行测试. 在训练期间没有看到GPT-5.4和Gemma-4。

blocks.en:
Although ToM2Vec is trained purely in self-play against a Qwen3-8B partner,
the observed gains on Overcooked persist when ToM2Vec is paired with unseen test-time partners ( Table 6 ).
With a strong GPT-5.4 partner, ToM2Vec improves over the base agent by 17.3 points on average, with positive gains on every layout. With a Gemma-4 partner the improvement is smaller but still persists.
This indicates that ToM2Vec learns a generalized model of partner reasoning rather than overfitting to its training-time partner.
This also highlights the generalizability of ToM2Vec to frontier model settings: we can train an agent against open-weight models and deploy it in teams with frontier models.
blocks.zh:
虽然TOM2Vec在对一个Qwen3-8B搭档进行自我游戏训练,
当TOM2Vec与未见的试验时间伙伴配对时,所观察到的超熟收益持续存在(表6)。
拥有强大的GPT-5.4合作伙伴TOM2 Vec比基剂平均提高17.3分,在每一布局上都有正面收益. 有了Gemma-4的合作伙伴,改进幅度较小,但仍在继续。
这表明TOM2Vec学习了一般的伙伴推理模式,而不是过于适合其培训时间伙伴.
这也凸显了TOM2Vec对前沿模型设置的通俗性:我们可以训练一种针对开放式模型的特工,并将其部署在具有前沿模型的团队中.

blocks.en: Table 7: Accuracy on Bayesian ToM probes in Overcooked. Beliefs : what the partner believes the agent is trying to do (a second-order inference). Desires : which subtask the partner is currently pursuing. Actions : which primitive action the partner will take next.
blocks.zh: 表7:超熟的贝叶斯TOM探测器上的精确度. 信仰:伴侣认为特工正在试图做的事情(二阶推论). Despeces:合作伙伴目前正在追求的次级任务。 动作:伙伴接下来会采取哪一种原始动作.

blocks.en:
Coordination scores alone do not reveal whether the latent tokens encode the components of a theory-of-mind: it could be that some improved performance comes from learning to predict information correlated with partner actions, without formulating a proper theory of the partner.
Thus, following the Bayesian Theory of Mind decomposition of an agent into beliefs, desires, and actions ( Baker et al., 2011 ) , we directly check each agent’s model of its partner with three questions at sampled Overcooked states ( Table 7 ). Belief questions ask the agent what it thinks its partner thinks the agent (i.e., itself) is trying to do. Desire questions ask the partner what it currently wants to do. Action questions ask which action the partner will take next.
Beliefs, desires, and actions each have six different options (based on the possible actions/steps within the Overcooked environment)
to choose from, making this a multiple-choice QA task, and test 300 samples per questions (see Appendix D for prompts).
We obtain ground truth labels by 1) continuing the partner’s generation and prompting it for its beliefs and desires and 2) directly taking the partner’s next action from its output. ToM2Vec achieves the highest accuracy on all three questions ( Table 7 ), improving over the next-best baseline by 5.6, 2.0, and 2.7 points.
The beliefs category is unsurprisingly the hardest question type for every method as it is a second-order ToM understanding capability (i.e., the agent must infer its partner’s theory about it).
blocks.zh:
仅靠协调得分并不能说明潜在的征兆是否编码了一种思维理论的构成部分:一些改进的绩效可能来自学习预测与伙伴行动有关的信息,而不对伙伴提出适当的理论。
因此,根据Bayesian的Mind理论,将一个代理人分解成信仰、欲望和行动(Baker等人,2011年),我们直接检查每个代理人的合伙人模式,并抽样调查三个问题。 超熟状态(表7). 信仰问题询问代理人认为其伴侣认为代理人(即自身)想做什么. 欲望问题询问伴侣当前想要做什么. 行动问题询问伙伴下一步将采取什么行动。
信仰、愿望和行动各有六种不同的选择(根据在过度拥挤的环境中可能采取的行动/步骤)
选择,使其成为一项多选择的QA任务,每个问题测试300个样本(提示见附录D)。
我们通过下列方式获得基本真理标签:(1) 继续伙伴的一代,促使伙伴的信仰和愿望;(2) 从产出中直接采取伙伴的下一步行动。 ToM2Vec在所有三个问题上都取得了最高的准确性(表7),比次佳基线提高了5.6,2.0和2.7点.
信仰类别是每一种方法最难处理的问题类型,因为它是二阶TOM理解能力(即代理人必须推断其伴侣对此的理论),这毫不奇怪。

blocks.en: Table 8: Perplexity of generated thoughts when trained by ToM2Vec across different types of thoughts. We test on the normal thoughts, altered layout (swapped real layout for alternate layout), and adversarial intent (partner agent is attempting to sabotage).
blocks.zh: 表8:通过TOM2Vec对不同类型思想进行培训后产生的思想的复杂性. 我们测试的是正常的想法、改变的布局(为另类布局而扭曲真实布局)和对抗意图(伙伴代理人正在试图破坏)。

blocks.en:
We compare the perplexity the model assigns to the partner’s true reasoning when the ToM latents are derived from the partner’s actual context against two deliberately corrupted contexts: Altered Layout, in which the current layout is replaced with a game state from another layout, and Adversarial Intent, in which the partner aims to hinder progress. The key assumption is that if the latents are capturing the partner’s reasoning, the generated thoughts from the true context should yield the lowest perplexity.
We find that the Normal latents reach a perplexity of 1.412, whereas both distractors are higher, at 1.702 and 1.613 for Altered Layout and Adversarial Intent respectively (see Table 8 ). Furthermore, the lowest perplexity is assigned to the correct CoT in 98.6% of cases with the true partner reasoning.
Corrupting the partner’s context degrades how well the latents predict its reasoning, indicating that the latents are sensitive to valid partner-specific information.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了模型给合伙人真实推理分配的迷惑性,当TOM潜伏物来自合伙人的实际背景,与两个故意腐败的背景: 变换版式,其中当前版式由另一个版式的游戏状态所取代,Adversarial Intent,其中合作伙伴旨在阻碍进步. 关键假设是,如果潜伏物能够捕捉到伙伴的推理,从真实背景中产生的想法应产生最小的困惑。
我们发现,正常潜伏物的迷惑性为1.412,而两个分散作用物的迷惑性都更高,分别是改变布局的1.702和1.613(见表8)。 此外,98.6%的病例中,有真实伴侣推理的,将最小的复杂度分配给正确的CoT。
使伴侣的背景受损会降低潜在因素对其推理的预测程度,表明潜在因素对有效的特定伴侣信息敏感。

blocks.en: 5 Related Work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en:
Theory of Mind is the capacity to infer the mental states of others, and is a cornerstone of human social cognition ( Premack and Woodruff, 1978 ) .
A long line of work explores ToM in non-LLM agents ( Gmytrasiewicz and Doshi, 2005 ; Pynadath and Marsella, 2005 ; Han and Gmytrasiewicz, 2018 ; Sequeira et al., 2025 ; He et al., 2025 ) , which we do not discuss in detail, as our scope is LLM agents.
In that context, a large body of work tested the ToM capabilities of varying models ( Le et al., 2019 ; Sap et al., 2022 ; Ullman, 2023 ; Kosinski, 2024 ; Xu et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2023 ) , showcasing where LLMs succeed and fail in different aspects of ToM.
Many past efforts have aimed to improve LLM ToM through inference-time prompting and decomposition, including perspective-taking prompts ( Moghaddam and Honey, 2023 ; Wilf et al., 2024 ) and structured decomposition of the inference into sub-problems ( Jung et al., 2024 ; Hou et al., 2024 ; Sarangi et al., 2025 ) .
A related line of work augments models with explicit symbolic belief-tracking structures ( Sclar et al., 2023 ; Xu et al., 2025a ; Tang and Belle, 2024 ) .
Outside of inference-time approaches, other previous approaches train LLMs to improve ToM ( Sclar et al., 2025 ; Hwang et al., 2025 ) .
In contrast to these efforts, ToM2Vec learns a latent partner representation supervised directly during self-play to facilitate broader understanding of the partner.
blocks.zh:
Mind理论是推断他人精神状态的能力,是人类社会认知的基石(Premack and Woodruff, 1978).
漫长的工作线在非LLM剂中探索Tom(Gmytrasiewicz和Doshi,2005年;Pynadath和Marsella,2005年;Han和Gmytrasiewicz,2018年;Sequeira等人,2025年;He等人,2025年),我们没有详细讨论,因为我们的范围是LLM剂.
在这方面,大量工作测试了不同模型的Tom能力(Le等人,2019年;Sap等人,2022年;Ullman,2023年;Kosinski,2019年)。 2024; 徐等人, 2024; Kim等人, 2023 ),展示LLMS在不同方面的成功和失败.
以往的许多努力都旨在通过推导和分解时间来改进LLM ToM, 包括取景提示(Moghaddam and Honey, 2023; Wilf等人, 2024 ),以及将推导分解为子问题的结构化(Jung等人, 2024 ;Hou等人, 2024 ; Sarangi等人, 2025 ).
一项相关的工作是用明确的象征性的信仰跟踪结构来扩大模式(Sclar等人,2023年;徐等人,2025年a;唐和贝勒,2024年)。
除推论时间办法外,其他以往办法都培训LLMs改进Tom(Sclar等人,2025年;Hwang等人,2025年)。
与这些努力形成对照的是,TOM2Vec学习了自我游戏时直接监督的潜在伙伴代表,以促进对伙伴的更广泛了解。

blocks.en:
A growing body of work has explored
latent reasoning.
A paradigmatic example of this is Coconut ( Hao et al., 2025 ) , which feeds the model’s last hidden state back as the next input embedding, allowing a single step to support several alternative continuations.
Subsequent methods have enabled latent thinking by adjusting how latent thoughts are trained ( Shen et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Su et al., 2025 ) .
Other attempts keep the model frozen and generate soft tokens that are projected into the LLM’s representation space ( Xu et al., 2025c ; Xu et al., 2025b ) or use probability-weighted embeddings ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) .
Additionally, Gozeten et al. (2025) show how continuous CoTs enable parallel exploration better than discrete CoTs.
Our work builds on prior work training latent reasoning models, especially findings that latent reasoning tokens can encode multiple paths. ToM2Vec is, to our knowledge, the first to explore this paradigm for modeling other agents, which poses distinct challenges (e.g., partial observability of other agents).
blocks.zh:
探索了越来越多的工作
潜在的推理。
一个典型的例子就是Coconut(Hao等人,2025年),它将模型最后隐藏状态反馈回作为下一个输入嵌入,允许单步支持几个替代续作.
随后的方法通过调整如何培训潜伏思想,使潜伏思考成为可能(Shen等人,2025年;Wu等人,2025年;Su等人,2025年)。
其他尝试使模型保持冷冻并生成软符,投射到LLM的表示空间(徐等人,2025c;徐等人,2025b)或使用概率加权嵌入(张等人,2026).
此外,Gozeten等人(2025年)展示了连续的CoT如何使平行勘探比离散的CoT更好。
我们的工作以以前的工作培训潜在推理模型为基础,特别是潜在推理符号可以编码多种路径的结论。 据我们所知,TOM2Vec是第一个为模拟其他物剂探索这种范式的人,它提出了不同的挑战(例如其他物剂的部分可观察性).

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced ToM2Vec , a ToM method that trains an agent via self-play to model its partner via continuous thought tokens.
Across five settings, both cooperative and competitive, ToM2Vec improves over all baselines and generalizes to partners not seen during training.
Analysis indicates that ToM2Vec is able to make more accurate inferences about the partner’s state, indicating stronger ToM understanding.
Taken together, the results suggest that modeling another agent in latent space is a useful alternative to doing so in text.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了TOM2Vec,一种TOM方法,通过自玩来训练一个代理,通过连续的思维符来建模其伴侣.
在合作和竞争的五个环境中,Tom2Vec在所有基线上都有改进,并向培训期间没有见到的伙伴概括介绍。
分析表明,TOM2Vec能够对伴侣的状态作出更准确的推断,表明对TOM的理解更强.
总而言之,结果表明,在潜在空间中建立另一种物剂的模型是一种有益的替代案文。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
ToM2Vec requires access to the partner’s CoT during training.
However, we show that this CoT does not need to come from the eventual test-time partner: training against one partner transfers to others.
Nevertheless, it is still a requirement of the training procedure, and our supervision relies on both agents sharing a representation space, which is why training uses the same base model for agent and partner. ToM2Vec also requires a training phase, unlike prompting-based approaches that work at inference time.
We find this cost is offset by performance, since the method outperforms both prompting and a training-matched verbalized baseline.
Finally, we note that our experiments use English-only tasks, a limitation shared with much prior work on LLM theory of mind and constrained in part by available models and datasets.
blocks.zh:
ToM2Vec 要求在培训期间使用伴侣的COT。
然而,我们表明,这种联合培训不需要来自最终的测试时间伙伴:针对一个伙伴转让给另一个伙伴的培训。
尽管如此,这仍然是培训程序的一项要求,我们的监督工作依靠双方的代理人共享一个代表空间,这就是为什么培训对代理人和伙伴使用同样的基模。 ToM2Vec还需要一个培训阶段,不同于在推断时间起作用的基于激励的方法.
我们认为,这一费用被业绩所抵消,因为这种方法的效绩既超过了提示性,也超过了培训时的口头基准。
最后,我们注意到,我们的实验使用了只使用英语的任务,这是与许多以前关于LLM思维理论的工作共同分担的局限性,并部分受到现有模型和数据集的限制。

blocks.en: Appendix B Dataset Details
blocks.zh: 附录B 数据集细节

blocks.en: • Overcooked-AI (MIT License): For each baseline, we run for 400 steps on the Cramped Room, Asymmetric Advantage, and Coordination Ring layouts for 30 different seeds. For training, we conduct self-play with a random agent to collect 4000 input game states to use during training across different timesteps. • Negotiation (MIT License): We generate 500 new negotiation settings with GPT-5.4 following the new task generation prompt in ( Abdelnabi et al., 2024 ) . Following the original paper, we allow discussion to proceed for 24 turns and take each turn except the last as a training sample. We conduct an 80/20 split on these samples to construct our training and validation data. • Decrypto (Creative Commons Public License): The original paper provides a list of 640 words to create a set of three keywords. For training, we create 1000 randomly sampled keyword sets and simultaneously use decoder and interceptor roles for training. For evaluation, we create another 1000 randomly sampled keyword sets. • Hanabi (MIT License): We train ToM2Vec over 4000 randomly generated Hanabi game states for input and do evaluation across 100 randomly initialized games of Hanabi. • Collab Escape/Capture (MIT License): We conduct self-play with random agents to to get input environment states for training for both Escape and Capture. We train ToM2Vec over 4000 input states for each setting and, following the evaluation scheme in the original paper, evaluate Collab Escape and Collab Capture on 12 and 6 seeds respectively.

blocks.en:
A more classic test of ToM is through reasoning on false agent beliefs.
More concretely, whether an agent can recognize that another agent holds a belief that differs from the true environment state. We evaluate this with a Sally-Anne style belief test ( Baron-Cohen et al., 1985 ) . To test this, we create a new Overcooked layout with custom “cupboard” tiles to test an agent’s ToM capabilities.
blocks.zh:
对Tom的更经典的考验是通过对虚假代理信仰的推理.
更具体地说,一个代理人是否能够承认另一个代理人持有一种不同于真实环境状态的信念. 我们用萨利-安恩风格的信仰测试来评价这一点(Baron-Cohen等人,1985年). 为了测试这一点, 我们用自定义的“ cupboard” 牌来创建一个新的 overcooked 版式来测试代理商的TOM 能力 。

blocks.en: A cupboard can be interacted with to store/retrieve an item, and the contents of a cupboard are not visible at all times (i.e., the content must be retrieved to reveal the stored item). We place eight cupboards along the edge of the layout and fill the remaining edge tiles with walls. To conduct this test, we have an overseer agent observe two players within the environment act following a set pattern. Player One takes three unique ingredients and stores each in three different cupboards. Player One exits and can no longer observe the scene. Player Two is given the item locations and chooses three random cupboards to move the ingredients to. Player Two exits, and player one enters. Now, given the game’s state history, we ask the overseer agent where it thinks Player One will look for each ingredient. We also independently ask the overseer agent where it believes the ingredients are after seeing them rearranged by player two to measure state understanding.
blocks.zh: 橱柜可以与存储/检索某个物品进行交互,橱柜的内容始终不可见(即必须检索内容以揭示存储的物品). 我们沿着布局的边缘放置8个橱柜,并用墙壁填满剩余的边缘瓷砖. 为了进行这次测试,我们有一个监督员特工 观察到环境行为中的两个玩家 遵循既定的模式。 玩家 一个需要三种独特的配料,每个都存放在三个不同的橱柜里. 玩家 一个出口,无法再观察现场. 玩家 二是给项目位置,选择三个随机的橱柜来移动成分. 玩家 两个出口,玩家一个进入。 现在,鉴于游戏的状态历史,我们问监督员认为玩家在哪里 一个会寻找每种成分。 我们还独立地询问监督者代理人,它相信这些成分是在看到它们被玩家二重排之后,用来测量状态理解的.

blocks.en: We conduct this test on 50 different seeds and find that ToM2Vec scores 0.88 ( Table 9 ), a 0.14 improvement over the untrained agent, tying Self-Consistency for the best result and outperforming all other baselines. We also note that state understanding stays relatively consistent among the different methods, differing by 0.08 at most. Since all the methods retain similar levels of state understanding, the gains in partner state understanding are due to enhanced ToM capabilities rather than better overall state understanding.
blocks.zh: 我们用50种不同的种子进行测试,发现TOM2Vec的分数是0.88(表9),比未受过训练的药剂有0.14的改进,将自我维持性与最佳结果挂钩,并且比所有其他基线都差。 我们还注意到,各国的理解在不同的方法之间相对一致,最多为0.08。 由于所有方法都保持了类似的州理解水平,伙伴州理解的提高是由于加强了Tom能力,而不是提高了总体状态理解.

Figure 3: We design a custom layout and collect five east/west CoTs where the partner (green hat) decides to go either east towards the dish dispenser or west towards the onion dispenser.
We calculate the perplexity of each CoT, plotted below. A high east perplexity indicates that a CoT corresponding to the dish dispenser is unlikely ; a low east perplexity means a dish CoT is likely, and vice versa for west and onions.

图3:我们设计一种定制布局,收集5个东/西CoT,伙伴(绿色帽子)决定向东或向西朝送菜器或向西朝送葱器。
我们计算每个CoT的复杂度, 如下图所示。 高东伸缩表示与菜肴喷洒器相对应的CoT不太可能;低东伸缩表示有菜肴CoT的可能性,反之亦然,适用于西洋洋葱.

blocks.en:
As a kind of theory, a theory-of-mind should be subject to rational revision given evidence.
In Section 1 we pointed to the latent nature of ToM2Vec as a core benefit in this regard: latent tokens more naturally lend themselves to representing multiple states, as has been shown for continuous reasoning tokens ( Hao et al., 2025 ) .
Here, we test the ability of the latent tokens learned by ToM2Vec training to update given observations.
Specifically, we construct a novel Overcooked layout, shown in Figure 3 , in which the agent (top, blue hat) and its partner (bottom, green hat) both start exactly in the middle, equidistant from the onion dispenser (west) and the dish dispenser (east).
We then sample partner CoTs corresponding to different partners, one instructed to go to the onions and the other to the dishes; we sample 5 CoTs per category.
Following our perplexity analysis in Table 8 , we compute the perplexity of these CoTs under the current set of latent tokens produced by the agent.
Crucially, we score these CoTs as we move the partner east (closer to the dishes) or west (closer to the onions).
blocks.zh:
作为一种理论,一个思想理论应该经过理性修正,给出证据.
在第一节中,我们指出TOM2Vec作为这方面核心利益的潜在性质:潜在标志更自然地可以代表多个国家,连续推理标志就表明了这一点(Hao等人,2025年)。
在这里,我们测试TOM2Vec训练所学到的潜在符号更新给定观测结果的能力.
具体来说,我们构思一部小说 图3显示的过度烹饪布局,其中代理商(上,蓝帽)及其搭档(下,绿帽)都从洋葱喷射器(西)和菜式喷射器(东)的中间,等距处完全开始.
然后,我们抽取合作伙伴与不同合作伙伴对应的CoT样本,一个被指示去洋葱,另一个被指示去盘子;我们抽取每个类别5个CoT样本.
根据表8中的复杂度分析,我们计算出这些CoT的复杂度,这是根据该剂目前产生的一套潜在符号。
关键是,当我们把伴侣移向东(靠近菜肴)或西(靠近洋葱)时,我们得分这些CoT.

blocks.en:
At each step, the agent observes the partner’s movement history, starting from the center.
A rational agent should update its theory about its partner based on its movement; while a priori the agent does not know whether the partner intends to go east or west, a series of movements east (towards the dishes) should raise the probability of dish CoTs (i.e., lower their perplexity) while lowering the onion probability, and vice versa. Figure 3 shows precisely this trend: as the partner moves closer to each dispenser, the corresponding perplexities shift as expected.
Promisingly, this indicates that not only does ToM2Vec teach agents to form snapshots of their partners, but it also teaches them to better update their theories given evidence.
blocks.zh:
每一步,代理人都会观察伴侣从中心开始的运动历史.
一个理性的代理人应该根据其运动来更新关于伴侣的理论;虽然先验的代理人不知道伴侣是打算向东还是向西走,但一系列向东移动(朝向菜盘)应该提高菜式CoTs的概率(即降低其迷惑度),同时降低葱的概率,反之亦然. 图3准确地显示了这一趋势:随着合作伙伴靠近每个投放器,相应的迷惑感会如预期的那样发生变化.
令人乐观的是,这表明TOM2Vec不仅教特工制作其伴侣的快照,而且还教他们更好地更新他们给出的证据的理论.

blocks.en: We evaluate ToM2Vec using paired t t -tests against each baseline over 30 matched random seeds on all tests Overcooked layouts ( Table 10 ) and 20 matched random seeds in Hanabi. At a significance threshold of p < 0.05 p<0.05 , ToM2Vec significantly outperforms the baselines in 16 of 18 cases on Overcooked. By Overcooked layout, it beats every baseline on the more complex Asymmetric Advantages and Coordination Ring layouts. On Cramped Room, the improvements are significant against all baselines except Self-Consistency and Adaptive ToM. For the negotiation deal success rate ( Table 11 ) and Decrypto win rates ( Table 12 ), we use a two-sided McNemar’s test ( McNemar, 1947 ) to compare each baseline to ToM2Vec . None of the five negotiation comparisons reaches statistical significance, likely to do insufficient sample size. For Decrypto win rate, ToM2Vec obtains statistically significant improvements in seven of 10 cases. Finally, we conduct a paired t t -test on 100 Hanabi seeds ( Table 13 ) and obtain statistically significant improvement over all baselines Language ToM.
blocks.zh: 我们用配对 t - t 的测试来评价 ToM2Vec。 过度烹饪的布局(表10)和20个匹配的花比随机种子. 在p < 0.05p < 0.05的重要阈值下,TOM2Vec在18个超熟病例中的16个大大超过了基线。 通过过度烹饪的布局,它比较复杂的不对称优势和协调环布局上的每一个基线都要好. 在密闭室,除自我维持和可适应的Tom外,对所有基线的改进都是重大的。 对于谈判成功率(表11)和德克里普托胜率(表12),我们使用麦克内马尔的双面测试(麦克内马尔,1947年)将每个基线与TOM2Vec进行比较. 5个谈判比较中没有一个具有统计意义,可能没有足够样本规模。 对于Decrypto胜率,TOM2Vec在统计学上显著改进了10个案例中的7个. 最后,我们对100个哈纳比种子(表13)进行双对t-t测试,并在统计学上大大改进了所有基线。

blocks.en: We provide information about ToM2Vec ’s compute details in Table 14 . We find that the added cost of ToM2Vec ’s continuous tokens is modest. At inference with the vanilla HuggingFace generation library on A6000 GPUs, emitting the 10 latent tokens adds 1150.1 ms per query on average (tested on 20 generation steps), corresponding to roughly 10 extra single-token forward passes before discrete generation begins. Note that this overhead is a fixed constant. Inference peak memory is unchanged (16.3 GB for both models), as the fixed latent tokens occupy a negligible amount of memory, given that the majority is still the model weights. The main cost is at training time (83.96 GB peak), but this is a one-time cost with no effect on test-time deployment.
blocks.zh: 我们提供TOM2Vec的计算细节。 我们发现TOM2Vec连续代币的附加成本并不高。 根据A6000 GPU上的香草HuggingFace一代库的推论,释放10个潜伏符号平均每个查询增加1150.1 ms(在20代步骤上测试),相当于离散生成开始前约10个额外的单键前传. 请注意,这种间接费用是一个固定的常数。 推算峰值内存不变(两种模型的16.3 GB),因为固定的潜伏符号占据了可忽略不计的内存量,因为大多数仍然是模型权重. 主要成本为训练时间(83.96GB峰值),但这是一次性成本,对试运行时间部署没有影响.

blocks.en: You are an agent playing the cooperative cooking game Overcooked. You control one player in a kitchen. Your goal is to cook and deliver soups as fast as possible. Game rules: - You earn reward only by DELIVERING soups whose ingredient set exactly matches one of the currently active orders. Each delivery yields a sparse reward (default 20, can vary per layout). - You will only be able to interact with dispensers, pots, counters, or serving areas once you are facing them. Movement actions turn you; INTERACT acts on the cell directly in front. - You can only hold ONE item at a time. To pick something else up, first place what you’re holding on a counter (X), or use it (drop ingredient into a pot, deliver soup at S, etc.). How to cook and serve a soup (the full loop): 1. PICK UP an ingredient: face an onion dispenser (O) or tomato dispenser (T) with empty hands and INTERACT. You now hold one onion / one tomato. 2. PLACE INGREDIENT IN POT: face a pot (P) and INTERACT. The ingredient drops into the pot. A pot holds at most 3 ingredients (’P1’ / ’P2’ / ’P3’ shown on the map). 3. START COOKING: once the pot has the ingredients you want (1, 2, or 3), face the pot and INTERACT with empty hands to begin cooking. The pot shows ’P1*’ / ’P2*’ / ’P3*’ while cooking and counts down (default 20 ticks; the prompt tells you ticks remaining). 4. GRAB A DISH: face a dish dispenser (D) with empty hands and INTERACT to hold a dish. 5. PLATE THE SOUP: face the cooking pot once it shows ’P!’ (ready) while holding a dish, then INTERACT. You now hold a soup with that pot’s ingredients. 6. DELIVER: face a serving area (S) while holding the soup and INTERACT. The order is fulfilled and reward is paid. Recipes / orders: - Only onions and tomatoes can be used as ingredients. A recipe is the multiset of ingredients in the pot when you start cooking it. Order matters NOT, but the set must match an active order exactly. Common recipes are 3 onions, 3 tomatoes, or mixes (e.g. 2 onion + 1 tomato). - The "Active orders" list in the game state shows every recipe currently worth delivering. Build the pot to match one of them before starting to cook. - Adding the wrong ingredient to a pot cannot be undone; once cooking starts, the recipe is locked. Coordination: - Two agents share the kitchen. Avoid blocking your partner or duplicating their work (e.g. both carrying onions to the same pot that’s already full). - Counters (X) can be used as a handoff: drop an item on a counter for your partner to pick up. Movement and facing: - A movement action (NORTH/SOUTH/EAST/WEST) ALWAYS updates your facing to that direction. After the action, your <dir> arrow on the map will point that way. - If the tile in that direction is walkable (’ . ’), you also move one cell there. - If that tile is blocked (counter, dispenser, pot, serving area, or another player), you DO NOT move -- you only turn to face it. Use this to line up an INTERACT. - To INTERACT with an object, you must first be facing it (the cell directly in front of your arrow). If you are not yet facing it, issue the direction action first to turn, then INTERACT on the next turn. - STAY leaves both your position and your facing unchanged. You will receive a 2D ASCII map of the kitchen state and your past action history each turn. Each cell is 3 characters wide. Column indices (x) are printed above and below the grid; row indices (y) flank each row on the left and right. Read any position as (x, y). Terrain cells (a single character centered with spaces): ’ . ’ = walkable floor          ’ X ’ = counter (can place items) ’ O ’ = onion dispenser         ’ T ’ = tomato dispenser ’ D ’ = dish dispenser          ’ P ’ = empty pot ’ S ’ = serving area Items sitting on counters / floor: ’ o ’ = onion   ’ t ’ = tomato   ’ d ’ = dish   ’ s ’ = soup Pots in use: ’P1 ’ / ’P2 ’ / ’P3 ’ = pot with 1 / 2 / 3 ingredients (not yet cooking) ’P1*’ / ’P2*’ / ’P3*’ = pot currently cooking with that many ingredients ’P! ’ = pot with a ready (cooked) soup Players occupy a 3-char cell ’<idx><dir><held>’: <idx>  = agent index (0 or 1) -- you will be told which one is you

blocks.en: You are an agent playing the cooperative cooking game Overcooked. You control one player in a kitchen. Your goal is to cook and deliver soups as fast as possible. Game rules: - You earn reward only by DELIVERING soups whose ingredient set exactly matches one of the currently active orders. Each delivery yields a sparse reward (default 20, can vary per layout). - You will only be able to interact with dispensers, pots, counters, or serving areas once you are facing them. Movement actions turn you; INTERACT acts on the cell directly in front. - You can only hold ONE item at a time. To pick something else up, first place what you’re holding on a counter (X), or use it (drop ingredient into a pot, deliver soup at S, etc.). How to cook and serve a soup (the full loop): 1. PICK UP an ingredient: face an onion dispenser (O) or tomato dispenser (T) with empty hands and INTERACT. You now hold one onion / one tomato. 2. PLACE INGREDIENT IN POT: face a pot (P) and INTERACT. The ingredient drops into the pot. A pot holds at most 3 ingredients (’P1’ / ’P2’ / ’P3’ shown on the map). 3. START COOKING: once the pot has the ingredients you want (1, 2, or 3), face the pot and INTERACT with empty hands to begin cooking. The pot shows ’P1*’ / ’P2*’ / ’P3*’ while cooking and counts down (default 20 ticks; the prompt tells you ticks remaining). 4. GRAB A DISH: face a dish dispenser (D) with empty hands and INTERACT to hold a dish. 5. PLATE THE SOUP: face the cooking pot once it shows ’P!’ (ready) while holding a dish, then INTERACT. You now hold a soup with that pot’s ingredients. 6. DELIVER: face a serving area (S) while holding the soup and INTERACT. The order is fulfilled and reward is paid. Recipes / orders: - Only onions and tomatoes can be used as ingredients. A recipe is the multiset of ingredients in the pot when you start cooking it. Order matters NOT, but the set must match an active order exactly. Common recipes are 3 onions, 3 tomatoes, or mixes (e.g. 2 onion + 1 tomato). - The "Active orders" list in the game state shows every recipe currently worth delivering. Build the pot to match one of them before starting to cook. - Adding the wrong ingredient to a pot cannot be undone; once cooking starts, the recipe is locked. Coordination: - Two agents share the kitchen. Avoid blocking your partner or duplicating their work (e.g. both carrying onions to the same pot that’s already full). - Counters (X) can be used as a handoff: drop an item on a counter for your partner to pick up. Movement and facing: - A movement action (NORTH/SOUTH/EAST/WEST) ALWAYS updates your facing to that direction. After the action, your <dir> arrow on the map will point that way. - If the tile in that direction is walkable (’ . ’), you also move one cell there. - If that tile is blocked (counter, dispenser, pot, serving area, or another player), you DO NOT move -- you only turn to face it. Use this to line up an INTERACT. - To INTERACT with an object, you must first be facing it (the cell directly in front of your arrow). If you are not yet facing it, issue the direction action first to turn, then INTERACT on the next turn. - STAY leaves both your position and your facing unchanged. You will receive a 2D ASCII map of the kitchen state and your past action history each turn. Each cell is 3 characters wide. Column indices (x) are printed above and below the grid; row indices (y) flank each row on the left and right. Read any position as (x, y). Terrain cells (a single character centered with spaces): ’ . ’ = walkable floor          ’ X ’ = counter (can place items) ’ O ’ = onion dispenser         ’ T ’ = tomato dispenser ’ D ’ = dish dispenser          ’ P ’ = empty pot ’ S ’ = serving area Items sitting on counters / floor: ’ o ’ = onion   ’ t ’ = tomato   ’ d ’ = dish   ’ s ’ = soup Pots in use: ’P1 ’ / ’P2 ’ / ’P3 ’ = pot with 1 / 2 / 3 ingredients (not yet cooking) ’P1*’ / ’P2*’ / ’P3*’ = pot currently cooking with that many ingredients ’P! ’ = pot with a ready (cooked) soup Players occupy a 3-char cell ’<idx><dir><held>’: <idx>  = agent index (0 or 1) -- you will be told which one is you
